primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Type 1 Bartter syndrome due to SLC12A1/NKCC2 loss of function
mechanism: Loss of the apical Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransporter NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb impairs sodium chloride reabsorption, reduces the lumen-positive potential that normally drives paracellular calcium reabsorption, activates renin-aldosterone signaling, and produces hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with hypercalciuria.
vignette: A child has polyuria, poor growth, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, elevated plasma renin and aldosterone, and hypercalciuria with nephrocalcinosis. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC12A1.
lead: Which nephron transport protein is directly affected in this disorder?
correct: The apical Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransporter in the thick ascending limb
distractors: The apical Na+-Cl− cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule
The epithelial sodium channel in collecting-duct principal cells
The basolateral Na+-K+ ATPase in proximal-tubule cells
The apical sodium-glucose cotransporter in the proximal tubule
distractor_notes: Loss of the distal-convoluted-tubule Na+-Cl− cotransporter causes Gitelman syndrome, which is classically associated with hypocalciuria rather than Bartter-type hypercalciuria.
Gain of epithelial sodium-channel activity causes Liddle syndrome with low renin and low aldosterone, not salt-wasting hyperreninemic Bartter syndrome.
Na+-K+ ATPase is ubiquitous in renal tubular transport; its generalized loss is not the SLC12A1-specific defect.
Proximal sodium-glucose cotransport is unrelated to the loop-diuretic-like salt-wasting and hypercalciuria phenotype.
key_expl: SLC12A1 encodes NKCC2, the apical Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransporter of the thick ascending limb. Loss of NKCC2 produces a loop-diuretic-like phenotype with renal salt wasting, renin/aldosterone activation, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, impaired concentrating ability, and increased urinary calcium because the lumen-positive voltage supporting paracellular calcium uptake is reduced.
objective: Identify NKCC2 loss in the thick ascending limb as the transport defect in type 1 Bartter syndrome.
